name: Word: Creating a Structured Thesis (CaST). Online
summary: This session is designed for researchers at the University of Queensland who need to use the complex features of Microsoft Word to structure complex documents.  It includes automation to limit repetitive tasks and meet the formatting requirements for a successful thesis submission.
details:
This workshop focuses on UQ's thesis submission requirements using formal documentation rather than generic skills-based training. However, this workshop is suitable for anyone seeking to learn about some of Word's more advanced formatting features.

At the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

  • Use styles with confidence
  • Apply automatic heading numbering
  • Generate automated tables of contents, figures, etc.
  • Insert captions and cross-references
  • Combine documents and merge formatting

The materials for this workshop are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

name: UQ R User Group (UQRUG)
summary: Skill-sharing and collaborative problem solving session for UQ's R user community
details:
R is a user-friendly programming language for statistical analysis, data visualisation and more.

UQRUG is UQ's R User Group: a monthly skill-sharing and collaborative problem-solving session for the UQ R user community. 

All skill levels welcome!

Our main purpose is to serve as a drop-in help session for help with R and RStudio, but to keep things interesting we will briefly highlight a useful method, tool, function or package each month. This month, Steph will run a quick introduction to the Positron IDE, as a recent additional alternative to RStudio and Spyder.

This is a hybrid event: you can join in person or online. To get the Zoom link, please book the event or contact training@library.uq.edu.au

Make sure to check out our UQRUG website (created with R and Quarto), and also join our UQRUG chatroom so we can keep helping each other outside the meetups.

This initiative is supported by the R-Ladies Brisbane Chapter and the UQ Library.

Please note we have a Code of Conduct.
venue: St Lucia, Duhig North Central Library (12), Training room 12-N109, and on Zoom

name: UQRDM for researchers and research students - how to use it to help with managing research data
summary: The session will explain best practice research data management using UQRDM to store, organise and share their research project related data and documents.
details:
The session will take researchers and research students step by step how to set up a research project record on UQRDM and to manage their research data and documents in accordance with policies, guidelines and requirements.

Please book in to receive session reminders and updates.

name: R with RStudio: getting started (in-person)
summary: A short introduction to R using RStudio. Hands on. No previous experience required.
details:
R is a popular programming language useful for statistics and data science.

What this session will cover:

  • Create a project for data analysis
  • Introduce useful functions
  • Working with scripts
  • Where to find help
  • Import data
  • Use a few shortcuts
  • Install and load extra packages
  • An example of data visualisation

The materials for this class are available on our website.
venue: St Lucia, Duhig Tower (2), 02-D217, Duhig Tower

name: Python Training (1 of 4): The Fundamentals
summary: Get started with Python and the Spyder IDE with this hands-on introductory session.
details:
Python is a programming language that is widely used for scientific programming. The Library offers this session to get you started with using Python for data science.

In this hands-on session directed at beginners, you will learn how to:

  • create a project
  • import useful modules
  • create variables
  • make use of functions
  • differentiate attributes and methods
  • import tabular data
  • visualise data
  • store code in a script

The materials for this class are available from our website.

name: R + dplyr: preparing data for analysis
summary: Transform your data with RStudio and dplyr in this hands-on R session.
details:
In this hands-on session, you will use RStudio and the dplyr package to manipulate your tabular data.

Specifically, you will learn about six dplyr "verbs" that can be used to:

  • filter data depending on conditions
  • sort data
  • remove variables
  • create new variables
  • collapse data to a summary
  • operate on separate groups

The materials for this class are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

It is recommended you attend a R with RStudio: getting started session before attending this one.

name: QGIS: Introduction to Map Making
summary: Create a custom map with a professional open source tool
details:
The Library offers a short introduction directed at beginners to get started using QGIS.

QGIS is a professional, open source Geographic Information System (GIS) that can be used to transform, visualise, analyse and publish spatial data.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:

  • load a basemap
  • import vector data
  • access a few sources of spatial data
  • join different data sets
  • personalise the look of the map
  • compose a print-out of your map

The materials for this workshop are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

name: Managing sensitive data
summary: How to manage and share sensitive research data in a safe and secured way
details: This workshop will look at what sensitive data is, how to manage sensitive data through the entire research project and 5 SAFE framework you can use to safely share and publish sensitive data.

name: GenAI Tools Overview: Uses and Nuances
summary: Explore various tools, their features and ethical considerations to make informed decisions about tool selection and usage
details:
This workshop introduces different Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools and their applications in academic work and studies. Learn about effective prompting strategies, literature searching, ethical considerations for AI use in your studies and a variety of tools for specific uses.

At the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

  • Apply effective prompting strategies
  • Use AI tools to enhance literature searching
  • Navigate integrity considerations when using GenAI
  • Understand privacy and ethical implications of AI tools
  • Identify appropriate AI tools for specific tasks

The workshop includes demonstrations of various AI tools including Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity, with a focus on their practical application in academic work.

name: Mastering prompt engineering
summary: This session will show you how to communicate effectively with Large Language Models (LLMs) to get higher quality, more accurate responses. Learn simple effective strategies and master the art of prompt engineering.
details:
Learn to communicate effectively with powerful Large Language Models (LLMs) like OpenAI's GPT-5 and Microsoft Copilot to get higher quality, more accurate responses. You don't have to be tech-savvy to create great prompts, join us to learn simple effective strategies and master the art of prompt engineering.

In this class, you will learn to:

  • Master Established Prompting Techniques: We will cover a range of established prompting techniques such as few-shot, chain-of-thought and persona prompting to give you a head start when working with artificial intelligence (AI). Gain the knowledge needed to take your prompts from simple questions to complex instructions.
  • Apply AI for Practical Tasks: We will explore practical prompt examples of how to use AI for research, study, problem solving and content creation.
  • Apply AI Ethically and Effectively: We will focus on responsible uses of AI to build your confidence and ethical awareness.

All are welcome. Come improve your AI skills with us!

This event is hosted as part of UQ Employability Week. For further information regarding the Week, and to explore the program, be sure to check-out our website: https://life.uq.edu.au/employability-week

details:

In this session, you will learn about:

  • Commonly used AI tools and models for writing code
  • Prompting strategies to get the best output

name: Open Access Publishing 101: How the Library can help!
summary: This workshop explores the pathways to open access publishing, and the support available through the UQ Library. It will demonstrate a collection of tools and resources that UQ Library has developed and designed to assist researchers to navigate the publishing process, to meet researchers strategic publishing goals and publish open access
details:
This webinar will discuss and demonstrate a collection of tools that UQ Library have developed to assist in strategic decision making about publishing and considering open access pathways as part of the process. The workshop will cover:

  • Open Access
  • Grant Funder Mandates
  • What is a Read and Publish Agreement and how do they work?
  • Council of Australian University Librarians (CAUL) agreements
  • Selecting a Journal
  • UQ Journal Search tool features and demonstration
  • Information/Instructions for Authors
  • Tips, tricks and what to look out for

These sessions are not recorded, slides and additional resources will be provided for those who attend.

name: Library Hack-AI-thon
summary: Join us at Central Library for a weekend hackathon where you'll team up with fellow students to tackle real-world challenges and develop solutions that harness the potential of artificial intelligence or address its risks. No coding experience required. Collaborate, create, and compete for prizes.
details:
Ready to tackle real-world challenges in the age of AI?

Join UQ Library and the Sustainable Innovators Club (SIC) for Hack-AI-thon - a weekend of creativity, collaboration, and big ideas. In teams of 3 to 5, you’ll work alongside fellow students to design bold, innovative solutions that harness the potential of AI or address its risks.

Come curious. Leave inspired.

What's the challenge?

You'll choose from eight challenges across five themes. The specific challenges will remain secret until the week of the event. Themes include:

  1. Strengthen Communities
  2. Educate and Empower
  3. Thrive Financially
  4. Care for Earth
  5. Nurture Wellbeing.

Create something impactful! From AI-powered apps, awareness campaigns, policy proposals or prototypes, the possibilities are endless.

No coding experience? No worries! This hackathon is open to students from all faculties and fields of study. Whether you're a thinker, designer, strategist or storyteller, your ideas and perspective are what matter most.

Event Details

  • When: 5pm, Friday 13 March to 5pm Sunday 15 March 2026
  • Where: Purple Stairs, Level 1, Central Library, UQ St Lucia
  • Who: open to all UQ students, organise your team beforehand or do it at the event

Register to attend. Entry is free. 

Enjoy the full hackathon experience for just $35. Purchase a hack-pack ticket and you'll get exclusive hackathon merch (lanyard, CV-ready certificate and laptop stickers) plus enough food to keep your brain innovating all weekend (think Subway, pizza and more). Payment required at registration. 

Sure, you can bring your own food...but let's be honest, our way is much more fun!  

Bonus perk! The first 80 hack-packs sold will score an exclusive Hack-AI-thon event t-shirt!

What to expect:

  • Hands-on problem solving
  • Expert mentoring
  • Networking opportunities
  • Pre-hackathon webinars, team-building and training events (see webpage for times)
  • Food all weekend (lunches, dinners and snacks) with the purchase of your hack-pack
  • A chance to create something meaningful
  • Prizes and bragging rights for the winning teams.

Further information: Check out the HackAIthon event page for your essential hackathon guide and the Terms and Conditions. 

Don't miss out! Spots are limited - register today.

Need support?

If you have any access or support requirements in order to participate fully in this event, please get in touch with the event organiser.

The Library has a limited number of sponsored hack-packs available for students with limited financial capacity. If this applies to you, please get in touch with us to discuss your circumstances.

Participants under the age of 18 years must have parental or legal guardian approval to enter this promotion. You must be 15 years or older to participate. 

This event is hosted as part of UQ Employability Week. For further information regarding the Week, and to explore the program, be sure to check-out the website.
venue: St Lucia, Central Library, Level 1, Central Library

name: R + Tidyverse: tidier data, simpler loops
summary: Learn about extra Tidyverse packages, including tidyr and purrr
details:
This session will help anyone dealing with a lot of data, that has experience with and looking to learn more about the R language and the Tidyverse dialect, using RStudio.

In this intermediate session, we will explore the purrr and tidyr packages to reorganise, manipulate and process data. We will also learn about how we can associate them with other Tidyverse functions from dplyr, ggplot2 and others.

The materials for this class are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

It is recommended that you are familiar with dplyr and ggplot2 before attending this session.

name: QGIS: Raster Analysis
summary: Intermediate session on processing and presenting raster data in QGIS
details:
Learn about acquiring, loading, processing and visualising raster data in QGIS, a professional, open source geographic information system.

In this session, you will learn to:

  • Style and process raster data
  • Troubleshoot common issues when importing spatial data
  • Use a Digital Elevation Model
  • Perform terrain analyses
  • Create a 3D map

The materials for this workshop are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

name: R  + tidyverse: tidier data, simpler loops(online)
summary: Learn about extra Tidyverse packages, including tidyr and purrr

The materials for this class are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

It is recommended you attend both R + ggplot2 (introduction and intermediate) sessions before attending this one.

name: Excel: Charting (online)
summary: Using Microsoft Excel chart tools to represent and visualise data.
details:
At the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

  • Distinguish between Charts and Graphs
  • Create a basic chart and template
  • Format and configure chart output
  • Represent Time, Frequency and Proportions
  • Combine Chart types

The materials for this workshop are available from our website.

name: Leveraging AI for Literature Searching
summary: This session will introduce you to the many new academic AI tools that have become available in recent years, and how best to use them
details:
There are many new artificial intelligence (AI) tools available to researchers and students which focus on academic sources. These tools offer a powerful new method of discovering academic literature. In this session you'll learn about the types of tools which are available, and the best techniques for finding the literature you need.

The workshop includes demonstrations and hands on exploration of various AI tools including SciSpace, Elicit and Perplexity.

name: Python Training (4 of 4): Statistics and further visualisation (online)
summary: This session is a continuation from the previous visualisation session, exploring the seaborn package in greater breadth and depth, by examining a broader range of plotting possibilities and visualisation options.
details:
In this session, you will learn how to use python to:

  • create distributive plots like histograms
  • create multi-plot visualisations with techniques like faceting
  • choose and create a variety of categorical plots
  • use colour to include additional information

This session will use Spyder. You should be familiar with Python.

It is strongly recommended to attend the “Python data visualisation with Spyder & seaborn” session first, as it covers foundational seaborn content. 

It is also recommended to attend the “Python with Spyder: Introduction to Data Science” and “Python data transformation and visualisation with pandas” sessions before this one.

name: GenAI Tools Overview: Uses and Nuances
summary: Explore various tools, their features and ethical considerations to make informed decisions about tool selection and usage
details:
This workshop introduces different Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools and their applications in academic work and studies. Learn about effective prompting strategies, literature searching, ethical considerations for AI use in your studies and a variety of tools for specific uses.

At the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

  • Apply effective prompting strategies
  • Use AI tools to enhance literature searching
  • Navigate integrity considerations when using GenAI
  • Understand privacy and ethical implications of AI tools
  • Identify appropriate AI tools for specific tasks

The workshop includes demonstrations of various AI tools including Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity, with a focus on their practical application in academic work.
venue: St Lucia, Duhig Tower (2), 02-D217, Duhig Tower

name: Mastering Prompt Engineering
summary: This session will show you how to communicate effectively with Large Language Models (LLMs) to get higher quality, more accurate responses. Learn simple effective strategies and master the art of prompt engineering.
details:
Learn to craft effective prompts that unlock the full potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, Claude, and Microsoft Copilot. No technical background required, learn practical strategies that deliver better, more accurate results.

In this hands-on session, you will:

  • Master proven prompting techniques including few-shot learning, chain-of-thought reasoning, and persona-based prompting to transform simple questions into sophisticated instructions
  • Apply AI to real academic tasks such as study planning, research, problem-solving, and content drafting
  • Navigate ethical considerations including proper attribution, bias awareness, fact-checking, and responsible AI use in academic contexts

Whether you're new to AI or looking to refine your skills, this session will equip you with practical applicable techniques to work more effectively with AI tools.

All experience levels welcome!
venue: St Lucia, Duhig Tower (2), 02-D217, Duhig Tower

name: Building your Python toolkit
summary: This session explores the building blocks of the Python programming language which will be useful for your toolkit. The focus will be on Python, rather than data, unlike our regular series.
details:
In this session, you will learn intermediate tools for effective Python programming, including

  • streamlining your code with control structures like conditionals
  • enabling iteration and automation with loops
  • building your own functions to simplify and modularise your code
  • understanding filesystems, environments and Python installations

This session will use Spyder, which you can access by installing the Anaconda distribution. It is expected you have some Python experience, we recommend attending our Python Training (1 of 4): The Fundamentals training first.

name: R + Quarto: reproducible publishing
summary: Create great-looking, reproducible documents and dashboards with R, RStudio and Quarto
details:
R is not limited to analysing data: you can use it in your project from importing to reporting.

Reproducible reports are integrated into RStudio, to make it easier to export a mix of code, outputs and prose to a variety of formats like PDF articles, websites, Word documents, slide decks and even dashboard.

In this session, you will learn about:

  • Why reproducibility can help you
  • Mixing code and prose
  • Formatting with Markdown
  • Exporting to different formats with Quarto
  • Updating a report in seconds
  • Creating a dashboard
  • Publishing to Quarto Pub

The materials for this class are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

It is recommended you attend a R with RStudio: getting started session before attending this one.

name: QGIS: Fieldwork Data Collection
summary: Create high-quality offline maps for use on your phone. Great for fieldwork and outdoor hobby activities.
details:
In this hands-on session, you will learn to:

  • access government spatial data and aerial photography
  • combine different data sets
  • create contours
  • utilise custom fields to simplify data collection in the field
  • use your map offline on your phone with QField

This session will use QGIS LTR version 3.40.x. Please install the software before joining this session.

You will also need to use your mobile phone, please download QField.

name: Word: Creating a Structured Thesis (CaST). Online
summary: This session is designed for researchers at the University of Queensland who need to use the complex features of Microsoft Word to structure complex documents.  It includes automation to limit repetitive tasks and meet the formatting requirements for a successful thesis submission.
details:
This workshop focuses on UQ's thesis submission requirements using formal documentation rather than generic skills-based training. However, this workshop is suitable for anyone seeking to learn about some of Word's more advanced formatting features.

At the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:

  • Use styles with confidence
  • Apply automatic heading numbering
  • Generate automated tables of contents, figures, etc.
  • Insert captions and cross-references
  • Combine documents and merge formatting

The materials for this workshop are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

name: OSM: create and extract geospatial data
summary: Learn how to contribute geographical data to OpenStreetMap, and use the database in QGIS.
details:
OpenStreetMap (OSM) is an open-licence spatial database.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn how to:

  • Digitise geographical data into the OSM database
  • Use an editor directly from the browser
  • Contribute local data as well as data useful to humanitarian action across the World
  • Make use of OSM data in QGIS to create a custom map

You do not need any prior knowledge to attend this session.

The materials for this workshop are available from the Software and training resources webpage.

summary: This online training via zoom will cover how to request a notebook in UQRDM, demonstrate major features and how best to use the notebook to work and manage your research data and documents.
details:
Digital Research Notebooks are a UQ wide digital solution that replaces paper based research notebooks and lab notebooks.  This online training will cover:

  1. Creating/accessing the notebook from within UQRDM and how to add collaborators
  2. Adding data to the notebook - notebook navigator, data entries, Office Online and the Office desktop plugin, widgets
  3. Managing data in the notebook - revision history, searching, tags, links, signing & witnessing

summary: Discover how to find grant money opportunities using the database Pivot-RP (formerly Research Professional).

name: Digital Research Notebook (LabArchives) for advanced users - session 1
summary: This workshop is designed for experienced users covering topics such as how to use Folder Monitor and MS Office and any new features.
details:
Michele Hosking from LabArchives will conduct this workshop focusing on using third party apps:

  • Folder Monitor: setting up rules and tips for new users
  • Microsoft Office: create and edit an existing Office files; save an Office file to your notebook and open an Office file from the notebook
  • Using ChemDoodle, SnapGene and GraphPad Prism
  • Jupyter notebooks: built-in viewer
  • PubMed Central: search and export citations

This is an online and hands-on workshop.  Please book in to receive session reminders and updates.

name: Digital Research Notebook (LabArchives) for advanced users - session 2
summary: This workshop is designed for experienced users covering topics such as how to use smart notebook features.
details:
Michele Hosking from LabArchives will conduct this workshop focusing on smart notebook features:

  • Organising the notebook: structure and scope, tips for best practice
  • Smart content: folder structure templates, page templates, data entry forms, copying from/to another notebook, copying within a notebook, cloning a notebook, linking related content, including content located outside the notebook 
  • Exporting notebook content: PDF copy and offline notebook

This is an online and hands-on workshop.  Please book in to receive session reminders and updates.

name: Digital Research Notebook (LabArchives) for advanced users - session 3
summary: This workshop is designed for experienced users covering topics such as how to do custom widget creation.
details:
Michele Hosking from LabArchives will conduct this workshop focusing on custom widget creation:

  • Built-in Widgets
  • Freezerbox and Database Widgets
  • The Widget Manager
  • Custom Widgets: simple data entry form, calculations in a widget
  • Sharing widget code

This is an online and hands-on workshop.  The attendees need to have an Administrator's right in order to perform tasks such as building a widget. 

Please book in to receive session reminders and updates.

name: Publishing datasets with UQRDM and eSpace
summary: Learn how to publish a dataset using UQRDM & UQ eSpace
details:
Journal editors frequently ask authors to publish datasets alongside their manuscripts. More and more funders are asking to make available the data generated from they sponsored research project. This session will:

  • outline the requirements for publishing a dataset
  • demonstrate how to publish a dataset via UQRDM to comply with journal and funder requirements
  • how to cite your published data

This is session is designed for current or experienced users of UQRDM.
